title: Shinnecock Outpost Tax Demonstrations
summary: The Shinnecock Outpost became a public assertion of Shinnecock sovereignty during 1997 organizing against renewed state tax pressure.
address_label: Shinnecock Indian Outpost, 42 Montauk Highway, Southampton, NY 11968
map_geometry_source: Public OSM/Nominatim location for Shinnecock Indian Outpost at 42 Montauk Highway; corrected from earlier rough Shinnecock Territory placeholder.
why_this_matters: This stop connects local Shinnecock action to wider Native coalitions across New York.
introduction_content: In 1997, Thom Little Bear Crippen, Shinnecock representatives, and the League of First Nations organized around state tax pressure and Native sovereignty. The Shinnecock Outpost made Shinnecock commercial and political authority visible on the landscape.
history_content:
The demonstrations connected local Shinnecock action with wider Native organizing across New York. Rather than treating the dispute as only a tax issue, Shinnecock representatives framed the outpost as a question of sovereignty, jurisdiction, and respect for Native nations.

Learning Questions

  • Why did Native leaders frame state taxation as a sovereignty issue?
  • How did the outpost make Shinnecock political authority visible on the landscape?
  • What is the difference between a business dispute and a jurisdiction dispute?

References

  • We Are Still Here: The Algonquian Peoples of Long Island Today.
